escena: SCENE (art direction pass on a beverage campaign, studio in Bogota, morning, NO faces): THE SUBJECT OF THE PHOTOGRAPH IS THE CORRECTION, NOT THE HAND THAT MADE IT — verify it by these landmarks: a large printed proof of a key visual for an unbranded craft juice, FILLING most of the frame edge to edge (we are close, the sheet is bigger than the picture), — a cold glass bottle with condensation, half-cut fruit and a band of headline space — lies on the worktop, seen at a steep angle so its paper grain and ink-blue halftone rosette are razor sharp; drawn ON TOP of it in thick ORANGE grease pencil are the marks of a creative director's review — a circle around the bottle, an arrow dragging the fruit across, a firm crossing-out on one element, a bracket in the margin. Those ORANGE marks are the SHARPEST, most deliberate, most contrasted thing in the picture and the eye lands on them first. The grease pencil itself lies on the sheet where it was put down; ANY hand is at most a blurred fragment leaving the frame at the far edge, never the subject. Hard window light rakes across the sheet from the right so the waxy ridge of each pencil stroke throws its own tiny shadow and reads as physical material. 100mm macro at f/5.6. The worktop around the sheet is BARE: NO mugs, NO plants, NO books, NO pens holders, NO laptop, NO people or faces in the background — only the proof, the pencil and the walnut. Everything is completely unbranded, no readable text anywhere — the marks are marks, not letters; the proof's headline band is blocks of tone, not words. COMPOSITION FOR A WEBSITE MENU (native to its frame): this vertical photo sits in the right column of a full-screen menu whose dark panel overlaps its LEFT third with a large curved corner at the top; so the SUBJECT and everything that carries the idea sits in the CENTRE-RIGHT of the frame, and the left third is calm continuation of the same scene, never empty and never a flat slab.

lecho.objeto: the out-of-focus near edge of the dark walnut worktop under the sheet
